video_title: The Stars of My New Movie "Best of The Best" - Maitreyi Ramakrishnan & Priyanka Kedia
gist: Comedian Hasan Minhaj interviews Maitreyi Ramakrishnan and Priyanka Kedia, the two leads of 'Best of the Best,' a Netflix film he co-wrote and co-produced with Prashant about the collegiate South Asian dance-competition circuit, releasing September 18, 2026 in 190 countries. The episode is mostly comedy bits, but it contains substantive detail on the five-year spec-to-screen studio gauntlet, Netflix casting and audition-tape process, four-month dance boot-camp training costs, and the commercial thesis that a 40-year-old diaspora subculture and female-friendship-centered storytelling are structurally underserved categories. Minhaj also discloses he is an investor in Kolkata Chai Company, where Kedia worked as a barista before being cast.

insights.claim: The Netflix film 'Best of the Best' launches globally day-and-date on September 18, 2026 in 190 countries with no theatrical window mentioned, the default streamer release pattern for mid-budget original films.
insights.speaker: Hasan Minhaj
insights.so_what: A simultaneous 190-country streaming release means all value accrues to subscriber engagement metrics rather than box office, so success signals for this category of film will only be visible via Netflix's own viewership disclosures.

insights.claim: Minhaj openly frames his own YouTube podcast episode as owned-media traffic generation to feed Netflix's recommendation algorithm, treating creator-controlled distribution as a substitute for paid marketing spend.
insights.speaker: Hasan Minhaj
insights.so_what: Talent with large owned audiences increasingly supplies its own marketing funnel, which lowers a streamer's P&A cost and raises the negotiating value of creator-producers relative to traditional actors.
insights.quote: And we need all the views that we can get to satisfy the Netflix ALGO gods.

insights.claim: Minhaj steers viewers toward Netflix's ad-free tier and characterizes the ad tier's inventory as dominated by GLP-1 drug commercials and unaffordable car ads, an on-the-record read of what ad-supported streaming currently monetizes.
insights.speaker: Hasan Minhaj
insights.so_what: Pharma (GLP-1) and auto being the perceived dominant advertisers on a major streaming ad tier is a read on where premium CTV ad dollars are concentrated and on the ad-load experience driving upgrade pressure.
insights.quote: Just be prepared to watch a lot of ads for GLP-1s and then a bunch of cars that you cannot afford.

insights.claim: 'Best of the Best' took Hasan Minhaj and his co-writer Prashant five years from going out on spec to release, with the project passing through a studio process where films are routinely shelved.
insights.speaker: Hasan Minhaj
insights.so_what: A five-year development cycle for a modest culturally specific comedy is a concrete measure of capital lock-up and optionality risk in streaming film development.
insights.quote: So Pashant and I we spent 5 years trying to get best of the best made. It went out on spec. Then it goes through the studio system gauntlet where your heart gets broken, it gets ripped apart. Sometimes a project will get sheld.

insights.claim: Even though Maitreyi Ramakrishnan was the producers' internal number-one choice from the outset, the studio still required her to complete a screen test, a studio test and chemistry reads before being cast.
insights.speaker: Hasan Minhaj
insights.so_what: Streamers impose formal casting de-risking even on producer-preferred, already-proven talent, which constrains how much creative control a creator-producer deal actually confers.

insights.claim: The studio's stated casting objection to Maitreyi Ramakrishnan was not acting ability but dance capability, and the producers had to argue that on-camera charisma could compensate for lack of technical dance training.
insights.speaker: Hasan Minhaj
insights.so_what: Skill gaps in genre-specific casting get resolved by post-cast training budgets rather than by casting trained performers, shifting risk into the production schedule.
insights.quote: But they were like, where's she at dance-wise?

insights.claim: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan argues the collegiate South Asian dance-competition circuit is a 40-year-old real subculture that Hollywood has left entirely unadapted while giving car racing roughly a dozen film franchises, framing it as a mispriced content category.
insights.speaker: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan
insights.so_what: Long-standing subcultures with built-in participant communities and no film canon are cheap IP-adjacent content with pre-existing audiences, a repeatable acquisition screen for streamers.
insights.quote: it's kind of crazy that people can get more fascinated by racing cars and give you like 12 movies about it or whatever how many but like this very real collegiate thing

insights.claim: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan's view is that a genuinely good underserved concept gets made eventually regardless of who holds it, meaning first-mover advantage in these categories is about timing rather than exclusivity.
insights.speaker: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan
insights.so_what: If underserved-category concepts are non-defensible, the return accrues to whoever executes first, favoring speed over long option-holding in development slates.
insights.quote: Good ideas will always float to the top. It will persevere.

insights.claim: Priyanka Kedia positions female friendship as a systematically underweighted narrative category in mainstream media, arguing romantic relationships are treated as the only valuable relationship worth centering a film on.
insights.speaker: Priyanka Kedia
insights.so_what: A platonic-friendship core rather than a romance core is an explicit product-differentiation bet aimed at a young female audience, and its performance is a test of whether that demographic under-serving is real.
insights.quote: I felt really frustrated with the narrative that relationships are the only valuable like romantic relationships are the only valuable relationships out there

insights.claim: The production staffed South Asian talent both in front of and behind the camera including director Lena, which Minhaj says is the first fully South Asian project he has worked on top to bottom, positioning end-to-end cultural authorship as the product rather than casting alone.
insights.speaker: Hasan Minhaj
insights.so_what: The differentiator being claimed is authorship depth, not diverse casting, which is a harder-to-replicate moat if the film performs.
insights.quote: everyone has hustled, everybody has had the door slammed in their face, everybody has heard no, everybody has struggled to see themselves represented anywhere

insights.claim: Priyanka Kedia was working as a barista at Kolkata Chai Company, a company Hasan Minhaj invests in, when cafe staff flagged her to him via Slack as an aspiring actress, and she was subsequently cast as a lead in a Netflix feature.
insights.speaker: Priyanka Kedia
insights.so_what: Lead casting pipelines still run on informal proximity networks rather than agency representation alone, which is why owning physical community hubs has real optionality for people in the business.
insights.quote: I was the personality hire. I was the girl that served you chai when you come home to the cafe.

insights.claim: The referral only produced a Slack flag to the producers; Netflix independently reviewed Kedia's unsolicited audition tape and separately identified her as a top pick before anyone connected her to the cafe.
insights.speaker: Prashant
insights.so_what: A referral that only buys attention while the tape does the selling is the structure that makes informal networks compatible with a studio's formal process, and it is how unrepresented talent actually breaks in.
insights.quote: So we were like going through audition tapes and yours stood out as we were like, "Oh my god, this person's amazing."

insights.claim: Steven Spielberg told Priyanka Kedia he personally handpicks every cast member and decides within ten seconds of watching an audition tape whether the performer has 'the sparkle,' a stated snap-judgment casting heuristic from a top-tier director.
insights.speaker: Priyanka Kedia
insights.so_what: If elite casting decisions resolve in ten seconds of tape, the first moments of a self-tape carry nearly all the value, which is a concrete allocation rule for anyone competing for these roles.
insights.quote: I watch your tapes and within 10 seconds I know if someone has the sparkle and that's how I decide

insights.claim: Kedia's agency database lists her as speaking conversational Hindi, which she admits on camera is false, illustrating that casting-database skill credentials are self-reported and routinely inflated.
insights.speaker: Priyanka Kedia
insights.so_what: Talent databases used for casting shortlists carry unverified skill claims, which is a quiet source of production risk when a role depends on a listed language or physical skill.
insights.quote: Listen, we all lie on our resume.

insights.claim: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan went through a four-month dance boot camp before formal training even began, a substantial pre-production investment made because the producers cast for charisma rather than existing dance skill.
insights.speaker: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan
insights.so_what: Casting a known name into a skill-dependent genre carries a months-long training line item that a studio must underwrite before a single frame is shot.
insights.quote: the rest of the choreographers that were teaching me throughout like that 4 month long boot camp before we even got to like training

insights.claim: The binding constraint in Ramakrishnan's training was physical stamina rather than choreography retention, with her brain able to recall the routines while her body could not sustain them.
insights.speaker: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan
insights.so_what: Conditioning, not learning speed, is the schedule risk when casting non-dancers into dance films, which argues for longer lead times rather than more rehearsal hours.
insights.quote: my brain was able to tell you the coro, but my body couldn't keep up because I just didn't have the stamina

insights.claim: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan runs a Twitch stream where she explicitly and repeatedly tells her audience the relationship is parasocial, and describes a self-policing community where other fans eject bad actors before moderators need to.
insights.speaker: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan
insights.so_what: Naming the parasocial dynamic out loud as a moderation tool is a low-cost community-health tactic, and community self-enforcement is what keeps creator moderation costs from scaling with audience size.
insights.quote: I constantly remind them that they don't actually know me. This is a parasocial vibe.

insights.claim: Ramakrishnan identifies the 'millennial pause' — unedited dead air at the start of a clip — as the single tell that triggers hostile engagement on short-form platforms, and credits professional editors with insulating older creators from it.
insights.speaker: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan
insights.so_what: Platform-native editing conventions are a real competitive input for creators crossing generational audiences, and paying for editors is how established talent buys past that gap.
insights.quote: Take out the millennial pause in your clips. That's going to save you from a lot of hate comments.

insights.claim: Hasan Minhaj discloses he is an investor in Kolkata Chai Company, which operates multiple flagship locations in New York City and also ships tea nationwide, and he promotes it with trackable checkout codes on his own podcast.
insights.speaker: Hasan Minhaj
insights.so_what: A celebrity-investor consumer brand combining owned retail with direct-to-consumer shipping and creator-attributed promo codes is a repeatable low-capital CPG structure worth watching in the South Asian food and beverage category.
insights.quote: I am an investor in a chai company called Kolkata Chai Company, which has numerous flagship locations here in New York City.

insights.claim: The cafe functions as an industry venue as well as a retail outlet, hosting the Deli Boys premiere party, and its staff are treated as a brand asset whose customer-relationship skill drives repeat business.
insights.speaker: Priyanka Kedia
insights.so_what: Physical hospitality locations that double as culture-industry gathering points generate deal flow and brand equity that a pure direct-to-consumer beverage company cannot buy.
insights.quote: Nobody leaves my cafe without a compliment.
